headline: New Jersey Turns Train Stations Into Unexpected Art Galleries
meta_description: NJ Transit's TRANSITional Art Project brings murals and photography to eight commuter stations, paying artists to create work that transforms daily commutes in…
summary_short: Since 2019, NJ Transit has installed temporary art exhibitions at eight stations, including a new show at Morris Plains Rail Station exploring 250 years of railroad hist…
body:
NJ Transit has discovered an unusual way to reach art audiences: place the work where people aren't looking for it. Since launching the TRANSITional Art Project in 2019 as a pilot at Newark Penn Station, the transit authority and New Jersey State Council on the Arts have installed temporary exhibitions at eight stations across the state, including Newark, Camden, Atlantic City, Trenton, New Brunswick, Summit, Rahway, and Morris Plains. The latest exhibition, "Tracks Through Time: Movement, History and Human Connection," features photography by Beyti Barbaros, murals by Jonathan Yumi, and a three-panel mural installation by Catherine Thurston, all examining 250 years of American history through the lens of railroads.

The brilliance of this approach lies in its recognition of a fundamental truth: most visitors to art galleries already chose to be there. A commuter glancing up at a mural while waiting for the 8:14 train didn't make that choice—and that unprompted encounter holds a different kind of power. Danielle Bursk, the State Arts Council's Director of Community Partnerships & Artist Services, describes it as an opportunity for people to "pause, connect, and see our communities in new ways" in spaces they move through every day.

Equally important, the program actually compensates artists. Rather than treating public art as volunteer work, NJ Transit provides stipends to help cover project development costs—a rarity in the public art world. By bringing art into the stations where the past and present intersect, the program transforms ordinary commutes into moments of unexpected discovery, reminding riders that beauty and history exist in the spaces we take for granted.
quick_facts: Eight NJ Transit stations now feature temporary art exhibitions
TRANSITional Art Project launched in 2019 at Newark Penn Station
Latest show explores 250 years of railroad and American history
Artists receive stipends for developing transit station projects
